rules.when: Research that needs current external facts: breaking news, current events, today's market or product state, release versions, or up-to-date documentation.
rules.why: Requires live web search, not frontier coding: Flash medium leads on Antigravity's large Flash pool, with Sol and Grok medium as fallbacks. Sonnet medium through Pi (Claude bridge or Antigravity's pool) spreads research load off Codex; the captain allowed Claude here on 2026-10-19, through Pi only, never the Claude Code harness.

rules.when: Task needs generated images or visual assets: icons, illustrations, logos, mockup art, placeholder imagery.
rules.why: Only Pi with pi-antigravity exposes generate_image; Flash medium avoids spending Argon's weekly reasoning pool on image calls.

rules.when: Review, audit, or second opinion on a diff/PR/design another crewmate produced. Not for writing the fix.
rules.why: Prefer a different model family than the author's: Argon for Sol-written work, Sol otherwise. Argon runs at high (Antigravity's ceiling) only in low-volume tiers because its weekly pool is small. Sol runs at xhigh because Sol high scores below Sol medium. Claude is not used for review: only Sonnet for research and read-only mapping and Haiku for evaluation judging, through Pi; Opus is reserved for the captain's own Claude Code session.

rules.when: Recon-only, file gathering, narrow lookup, or a trivial mechanical edit (rename, format sweep, typo fix). Not for research that needs current external facts.
rules.why: Trivial effort: use the cheapest low-effort models (Luna and Flash) so the workhorse Codex and Argon reasoning pools are not spent here.

rules.when: Ordinary implementation, bounded bug fix, tests, everyday coding with a clear path.
rules.why: Sol medium leads high-volume coding at the lowest cost and time per task; Argon is reserved for harder, low-volume tiers, with Grok medium as fallback.

rules.when: Large/ambiguous multi-file change, risky refactor, work holding many moving parts at once.
rules.why: Sol xhigh leads on cost and speed near frontier quality, with Argon high (Antigravity's ceiling) second and Grok xhigh as fallback. Sol runs at xhigh because Sol high scores below Sol medium.

rules.when: Hardest available work: root-cause investigation, architecture, ambiguous design, or already failed on the workhorse tier.
rules.why: Frontier reasoning for work that justifies maximum cost: Sol xhigh and Argon high (Antigravity's ceiling) are the strongest non-Claude profiles. Claude is not used here: only Sonnet for research and read-only mapping and Haiku for evaluation judging, through Pi; Opus is reserved for the captain's own Claude Code session.

rules.when: Read-only mapping of an existing application or codebase: as-built feature maps, capability inventories and where-is-it surveys that produce a report and change no files.
rules.why: Careful reading across many files without edits: Sonnet medium through Pi (Claude bridge or Antigravity's pool) and Sol medium; the captain allowed Claude Sonnet for research and mapping on 2026-10-19, through Pi only, to spread load off Codex.

rules.when: Evaluation judging: score finished outputs, runs or transcripts against a fixed rubric as the judge in an evaluation loop. Not for reviewing or writing code.
rules.why: The captain chose Haiku for evaluators on 2026-10-19: a small, different-family judge for Codex-authored work, through Pi only; Luna medium is the fallback.
